-Supermodularity at A ⊓ B and B ⊓ C bounds the sum of their values by f B + f (A ⊓ C). Supermodularity of the reciprocal at A ⊔ B and B ⊔ C bounds the sum of the reciprocal values by 1 / f B + 1 / f (A ⊔ C). Monotonicity also bounds each meet value by f B and each reciprocal join value by 1 / f B. Ordering the two reciprocal weights and splitting at f (A ⊓ C) ≤ f B gives the scalar estimate needed for the triangle inequality. No distributive law or complement enters this argument.
+Supermodularity at A ⊓ B and B ⊓ C bounds the sum of their values by f B + f (A ⊓ C). Supermodularity of the reciprocal at A ⊔ B and B ⊔ C bounds the sum of the reciprocal values by 1 / f B + 1 / f (A ⊔ C). Monotonicity also bounds each meet value by f B and each reciprocal join value by 1 / f B. Ordering the two reciprocal weights and splitting at f (A ⊓ C) ≤ f B gives the scalar estimate needed for the triangle inequality. No distributive law or complement enters this argument. In equation (1.4) of Born-weighted Jaccard projection geometry, the converse is the positive-denominator normalization of three triangle substitutions. For A<=B, the triangle with endpoints A,A and middle B reads 0<=2(1-f(A)/f(B)), giving f(A)<=f(B). For arbitrary A,B put a=f(A), b=f(B), u=f(A join B), and t=f(A meet B), all strictly positive. The join-middle triangle reads 1-t/u<=(1-a/u)+(1-b/u), equivalent to a+b<=u+t. The meet-middle triangle reads 1-t/u<=(1-t/a)+(1-t/b); dividing its rearrangement by t gives 1/a+1/b<=1/t+1/u. These substitutions recover Mon(f), Sup(f) and Sup(1/f); resultSufficiency supplies the forward application from these hypotheses to every triangle. Together with monotonicity, modularity and positivity also supply reciprocal supermodularity: monotonicity puts a,b in [t,u], and a+b=t+u gives t*u<=a*b, hence 1/a+1/b<=1/t+1/u. This is the parameter correspondence for the supplied criterion, with no zero-bottom extension and no additional Lean declaration. The cited B1 Theorems 1 and 4 remain literature inputs; the declaration resultSufficiency has exactly the sufficiency type displayed here.
 
 **Theorem 1.9 (Log-submodularity also suffices on every lattice).**

@@ -24,6 +24,16 @@ A nonscalar Hermitian operator has unequal eigenvalues M>m>0 on orthonormal vect
 
 For separation, the difference of projections onto two strictly nested subspaces is an orthogonal projection onto a nonzero subspace. Its trace pairing with a faithful state is positive, so mu is strictly monotone. Equality of the meet and join weights therefore forces the two subspaces to coincide. These arguments formalize the tracial classification application in Corollary 4.1 of Born-weighted Jaccard projection geometry. They make no literature originality claim and do not include the separate sharp interval supremum or nonattainment assertions. All statements are general parameterized theorems, rather than finite computations or certified numerical instances.
 
+For Corollary 4.2 use any index type I and the actual family P:I->End(H) of pairwise commuting orthogonal projections. Pinned Mathlib LinearMap.IsSymmetric.iSup_iInf_eq_top_of_commute and directSum_isInternal_of_pairwise_commute, in Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/JointEigenspace.lean, accept arbitrary I; no finite-family assumption is needed. Set H(chi)=the intersection of the eigenspaces of P(i) at chi(i). orthogonalFamily_iInf_eigenspaces makes distinct such blocks orthogonal. Its independent nonzero subfamily is finite by iSupIndep.fintypeNeBotOfFiniteDimensional, with at most n members by iSupIndep.subtype_ne_bot_le_finrank in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dimension/Finite.lean. These interfaces use revision 56a005855ea17e0b0958f73ec801ae140b0a1679. The empty family and the all-scalar family give one nonzero block H, and indistinguishable coordinates remain in the same joint block.
+
+Idempotence forces each chi(i) on a nonzero block to be 0 or 1. Each generator is consequently the orthogonal sum of its 1-blocks. Finite sums, intersections and orthogonal complements of these block sums correspond to union, intersection and complement of their index subsets, so every event in the original generated Boolean algebra is such a sum. For the nonzero blocks set p(chi)=weight rho H(chi). weight_pos and native_matrix_faithfulness give p(chi)>0. Repeated weight_orthogonal_sup gives mu(event)=the sum of its p(chi), and the full sum is Tr(rho)=1. Thus f_c on this same event algebra is nonnegative, monotone and modular. modular_nonnegative_triangle applies for every c>=0, including its zero-pair branch; faithful_separation, distance_properties restrict to the event algebra and give the remaining metric axioms. This uses the one actual rho throughout, without any commutation of rho with the family. K1 Theorem 3 also permits a nonnegative constant at the empty set; its citation is separate from the Lean suppliers.
+
+For Proposition 5.1, weight_orthogonal_sup is orthogonal additivity and weight_strictMono is strict inclusion. In the scalar case the projection trace identity LinearMap.IsProj.trace and Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq give full modularity. In the nonscalar case use the one orthonormal eigenbasis from the spectral construction in operator_classification: equal eigenvalues would give a scalar operator by basis extensionality and trace one, so some pair has M>m>0. Apply BornJaccardFixedOverlap.pair_construction at any 0<r<1 to those two eigenvectors. Its simultaneous line weights, actual zero meet and actual join T, together with weight_orthogonal_sup, normalize to f_c(R+L)+f_c(R+N)-f_c(R+T)-f_c(R)=r(M-m)>0. This disproves supermodularity and hence modularity. interval_defect gives positive triangle defect r(M-m)/(c+mu(R)+M+m).
+
+When n>=3, Fin.exists_ne_and_ne_of_two_lt supplies a third distinct index in that same eigenbasis. Let R be its nonzero eigenline and T the span of the unequal-eigenvalue pair. Orthonormality gives T<=R.orthogonal and dim(T)=2. At c=0, weight_pos gives mu(R)>0 and weight_strictMono gives f_0(X)>=mu(R)>0 for every X in [R,R+T]. The same pair_construction and interval_defect give the violation inside this strictly positive interval. When n=2 take R=0 and T=H; the violation remains valid with the original zero-bottom convention. No representation theorem for arbitrary two-dimensional measures is used. These are parameter choices in the existing spectral and fixed-overlap suppliers, with no added theorem or enlargement of the optimization domain.
+
+For Proposition 5.2, LinearMap.IsProj.trace identifies the ordinary projector trace with dim(X). scalar_triangle and modular_nonnegative_triangle supply the unweighted trace metric after positive rescaling: c+dim(X) is n times c/n+dim(X)/n, so the quotient and zero-pair convention agree; at c=0 normalized and ordinary trace give the same metric. Equation (1.4) retains its strictly positive valuation hypotheses and the triangle substitutions described in BadicaJaccardArbitraryLattices. Proposition 5.1 above identifies the modularity obstruction for nonscalar Born weights, including the positive-bottom interval at n>=3, while the commuting-event argument retains Corollary 4.2. The source references B1 and G1 are cited inputs: Gleason's Theorem 4.1 concerns orthogonal additivity in separable real or complex dimension at least three and a positive semidefinite trace-class representation. It supplies neither arbitrary-pair modularity nor faithfulness. All metric and separation applications here keep the finite faithful density hypotheses; no singular-state or infinite-dimensional conclusion is inferred.
+
